newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares, driven by IPO demand, end weaker.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares, driven by IPO demand, end weaker.

text.p: Singapore shares were driven by retail interest in debutant stock Tye Soon on Monday while funds were largely sidelined awaiting trade figures, dealers said.
The release of Singapore's April non-oil export figures and the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy meeting on Tuesday followed by the Vesak Day holiday on Wednesday, thinned buying interest.
"There was better volume in the afternoon, mainly from bargain-hunters," said a dealer with a local bank. But he said a major institutional presence was absent.
The Straits Times Industrials Index ended 9.56 points lower at 2,050.94, on a moderate turnover of 120 million shares.
Automotive component distributor Tye Soon ended at Singapore 48 cents, down from a 55-cent high on a volume of 32.6 million.

Malaysia'a MBF Capital drew strong interest, rising S$0.17 cents to S$2.61 on persistant rumours of a merger with Suria Capital. Singapore Telecom shed six cents to S$2.47, continuing a fall resulting from the loss of its monopoly on April 1.
Gainers included some foreign tranches of banks like UOB and DBS, which rose 30 cents to S$15 and S$18.40 respectively.
